_about: THE STANDARD for "tools worth knowing": the real run of 15 Oct 2026, 13 tools, as stored. Public products and public review pages only.

tools.name: Carrd
tools.what_it_does: Single-page site builder for landing pages, portfolios, and product hubs. Mobile-first, minimal design.
tools.price_note: Free tier very limited; Pro tier extremely cheap
tools.instead_of: Wix, Webflow, WordPress for simple landing pages
tools.verdict: Default MVP landing page for indie creators. Fast setup (minutes), mobile-friendly out of box. Limitation: one page only, no email automation built-in.
tools.evidence: 2.5M sites built (Carrd AMA on Indie Hackers 2024), mentioned across Substack creator workflows and Twitter indie community, 13.6M monthly visits (Feb 2026)

tools.name: Gumroad
tools.what_it_does: Host and sell digital products (ebooks, courses, software). Unlimited email list. Free customer updates.
tools.instead_of: Building custom payment processing and fulfillment infrastructure; Stripe + custom code
tools.verdict: Founder interviews show the real workflow: tease on social → email list → launch to email list → gather feedback. Low friction for creators without engineering resources.
tools.evidence: Founder case studies from course creator guides; Gumroad founder Sahil Lavingia interviews about growth from one-on-one creator outreach

tools.name: Lemon Squeezy
tools.what_it_does: Digital product sales with merchant-of-record (handles tax/VAT). Abandoned cart emails for subscriptions.
tools.verdict: Solves tax/VAT headache that Gumroad doesn't. Approval process documented as frustration point (slows launches). Fee structure (5% + $0.50) is higher on low-priced items than Gumroad. Email features more limited.
tools.evidence: Multiple 2024-2026 comparisons from indie creators (ByBurk, Velox Themes, WeCareFounders); approval delays mentioned across indie forums

tools.name: ConvertKit (Kit)
tools.what_it_does: Email marketing and automation for creators. Product launch sequences, welcome funnels, subscriber segmentation.
tools.verdict: Designed for creator economics (product launches, segmentation). Creators pair with Substack for automation depth. Real gotcha: higher pricing than alternatives; requires custom integrations for digital product workflows.
tools.evidence: Multiple practitioner blogs and comparison articles from SequenzY and Mailtoolfinder; creator launch workflows documented

tools.name: Typeform
tools.what_it_does: Customer discovery via surveys and forms. Validate ideas, collect feedback before building.
tools.price_note: Free tier capped at 10 responses/month; paid starts $25-29/month
tools.verdict: Recommended in 3-5 question format for customer validation. Real gotcha: free tier is punishing (10 responses only); branching logic restricted to paid. Practitioners recommend 5-question screener format.
tools.evidence: Multiple indie-focused guides (Ideaplan, Koji, EarlyCustomers, IndieTools); recommended in practitioner customer-discovery playbooks

tools.name: Zapier
tools.what_it_does: No-code automation. Connect form submissions → email lists → CRM → follow-up sequences without code.
tools.price_note: Free tier ~100 tasks/month; paid $10-20+/month depending on complexity
tools.verdict: Standard for indie automation stacks (forms → Airtable → Gmail). Real gotcha: free tier exhausts fast with multi-step automations; GDPR/consent handling not covered in free tier docs.
tools.evidence: Airtable's own support docs, indie automation guides (Calmops), Switch Labs tutorials, documented in Substack/Airtable workflows

tools.name: Make (formerly Integromat)
tools.what_it_does: No-code automation platform. Similar to Zapier but with more flexible workflow logic.
tools.verdict: More flexible workflow logic than Zapier for complex automations. Real gotcha: free tier exhausts quickly; pricing per operation can surprise.
tools.evidence: Mentioned in Switch Labs tutorials and Calmops indie automation guides as Zapier alternative

tools.name: Brevo (formerly Sendinblue)
tools.what_it_does: Email and SMS marketing with automation. Billed by emails sent, not contacts stored.
tools.verdict: Indie hackers appreciate free tier (300/day, SMS included). Real gotcha: automation setup takes 2-3 hours; interface feels dated vs Mailchimp/ConvertKit. Steep jump from free to Professional plan pricing.
tools.evidence: IndieRadar review (indie-focused), HackAcceleration review, multiple 2026 reviews from practitioner sites

tools.name: Airtable
tools.what_it_does: Customer database and light CRM. Organize customer data, manage relationships, track orders. Integrates with Zapier for automation.
tools.price_note: Free for individuals/small teams; paid from ~$12/month
tools.verdict: Standard database for indie stacks (paired with Zapier for email automation). Lacks built-in email automation. Scales but breakdowns noted above ~100 customers without optimization.
tools.evidence: Airtable case study (Halo Cars), community forum discussions, multiple indie guides; standard in documented Zapier workflows

tools.name: BuzzStream
tools.what_it_does: Relationship management and outreach tracking. Organize prospects by campaign/sector/client. Tracks contact history, follow-ups, link status.
tools.price_note: Pricing not disclosed; contact for quote (typical for larger agencies)
tools.verdict: UNPROVEN — Built for relationship tracking at scale (30+ simultaneous campaigns). Real usage: Content Customs manages tens of thousands of contacts. Real limitation: case studies lack independent verification; UI complex for new users..
tools.evidence: The only source found was the vendor's own site.

tools.name: Postaga
tools.what_it_does: AI-assisted link building. Analyzes site, suggests campaigns (skyscraper, guest post, resource page), finds prospects, builds personalized outreach sequences.
tools.price_note: Conflicting reports: sources cite $29+/month or free tier available—verify current
tools.verdict: AI campaign suggestions and preset templates. Designed for solopreneurs/small teams (raised $180K from TinySeed accelerator per Indie Hackers). Real limitation: indie-hacker positioning suggests smaller target audience; limited independent reviews. Pricing unclear.
tools.evidence: Indie Hackers coverage by founders (Andy Cabasso, Sam Brodie); positioned as fast setup for independent operators

tools.name: Respona
tools.what_it_does: Automated prospecting and outreach with AI personalization. Finds link prospects, generates icebreakers, manages campaigns via credits.
tools.verdict: UNPROVEN — AI personalization praised for sounding human. Automation runs at scale. Case study: 1,000 guest post pitches → 20.5% response rate → 55 placements. Real gotcha: credits system 'burns through budget fast' per reviewers; occasional bugs with domain authority filtering; email verification issues on niche domains..
tools.evidence: The only source found was the vendor's own site.

tools.name: Majestic
tools.what_it_does: Specialist backlink analysis. Trust Flow and Citation Flow metrics assess link quality. Link Context shows where links appear on page.
tools.instead_of: Ahrefs (for quality assessment specialists), Semrush (quality metrics focus)
tools.verdict: Specialist tool for backlink quality assessment. Trust/Citation Flow ratio (0.5–1.5 healthy) used by professionals. Real limitation: does not do keyword research or general SEO; smaller index than Ahrefs; requires pairing with other tools.
tools.evidence: PageOnepower guide recommends workflow (TF/CF ratio → Topical Trust Flow → Link Context); paired with Ahrefs by teams doing deep analysis
